chunks: Al-Husayn ibn Ibrahim ibn Ahmad ibn Hisham al-Mukattib - may God be pleased with him - narrated that Abul Husayn Muhammad ibn Ja'far al-Kufi al-Asadi said: Muhammad ibn Isma'il al-Barmaki narrated to us, Al-Husayn ibn al-Hasan, from Bakr ibn Salih, from al-Hasan ibn Sa'id, from Abul Hasan al-Rida (peace be upon him)
Regarding His saying, Exalted and Mighty is He: 'The Day that the shin shall be laid bare, and they shall be summoned to prostration,'
He said: A veil of light is removed, so the believers fall in prostration, and the backs of the hypocrites become rigid/stiffened so they cannot prostrate.

key_terms.يَدْعُونَ إِلَى السُّجُودِ: They shall be summoned to prostration
key_terms.يَوْمَ يُكْشَفُ عَنْ ساقٍ: The Day that the shin shall be laid bare

ai.seo_question: What is the meaning of 'The Day that the shin shall be laid bare' in Shia interpretation?
ai.summary: Imam al-Rida (peace be upon him) interprets the 'shin' (sāq) in Surah Al-Qamar as a veil of light that is removed on the Day of Resurrection, creating a natural inclination for believers to prostrate in awe. Conversely, this same divine revelation causes the backs of hypocrites to stiffen, physically preventing them from prostrating despite their desire. This interpretation highlights the physical manifestation of spiritual states in the Hereafter, a concept deeply rooted in Shia exegetical tradition.
